results.title: A risk management plan for CubeSats
results.abstract: Risk management is a crucial step of any spacecraft design in order to ensure system functionality and mission success. Unfortunately, risk management plans are typically high-level descriptions of risk philosophies or are too detailed for use on a student-built or otherwise low-budget spacecraft design. This paper outlines a risk management plan for CubeSats by first identifying risks, defining the root causes and their priority, and naming a responsible party for monitoring the root cause. These mission risks are then ranked by their likelihood and consequence of occurrence. Rationales for these rankings and the graphing of the mission risk on a 5x5 grid complete the risk identification phase of this risk management plan. To monitor the progress of the mission risks throughout the design life cycle, four types of mitigation strategies are described and risks are re-evaluated at key design milestones. Each step of this risk management plan is described and an example given based upon the risk analysis completed for a 3U CubeSat being built by a student team at The University of Texas at Austin. The paper then concludes with the proposed future work of gathering previously flown CubeSat mission failures through a Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA) within a Probabilistic Risk Assessment (PRA). © 2012 by the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Inc. All rights reserved.

results.title: Using AADL to enable MBSE for NASA space mission operations
results.abstract: This paper describes the potential of Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) that uses the Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) to model space systems. AADL modeling is applicable to real-time embedded systems- the types of systems NASA builds. A case study with the Juno mission to Jupiter showcases how this work will enable future missions to benefit from using these models throughout their life cycle from design to flight operations. © 2014 California Institute of Technology. Government sponsorship acknowledged.
